items.reason: Pinning a tag to a digest requires asking GitHub what each tag points at, and this session has no network; the repository already ships the exact tooling (`npm run actions:pin`, which rewrites the workflows AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass) plus a blocking `actions:check` inside check:ci, so the only missing step is one networked run.

Deciding which landing path those subjects took needs git history and CI run logs, neither of which this session has; A5 is wired in both places the repo lands changes (agent-review.yml on push/PR against `github.event.before`, and `review:agent:gate` inside check:ci via .husky/pre-push), and AGENTS.md already records the residual cause — an outer lane composing the subject from a report's first line in a hookless worktree — as having no repository-side fix.

Already covered: .github/constraint-map.json plus the AGENTS.md table 'Which of these rules will actually stop you' is exactly that index (52 rules, each with a rung of blocking/reporting/partial/honour and the fence that backs it), and test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs blocks when a claimed fence does not exist, when a quoted rule has moved, when the two halves disagree, or when a check:ci stage has no rule attached; the scan sampled CLAUDE.md and eslint.config.mjs rather than AGENTS.md.

The mutation catalogue now covers the two seams the item names — the LLM chokepoint and the store seam — with four new mutants, per-seam floors, MUTANT_FLOOR raised 7 to 11 and the matching floor.min pinned in the contract ledger, so the floors block on every build via test-unit/mutation-census.test.mjs and a survivor fails the weekly drill.

Already covered: .github/workflows/post-deploy.yml runs on the same push that releases, waits for the deployment to answer and probes /api/health behind the constant-time CRON_SECRET guard, records skipped-with-a-reason rather than an unearned green when a key or the URL is absent (declared in scripts/harness-degradation.mjs and drilled by harness:drill), keeps the verdict for 90 days, and deliberately does not hold a token that could revert.

Added .github/autonomy-budget.json (the triage owner and cadence, a maxUnreadDays, all eight unattended lanes with what each can write, five change classes that wait for a human whatever the gate says) and scripts/autonomy.mjs, whose pauseState() is now read by scripts/issue-dispatch.mjs --gate before the event is parsed or a model is called — so the pause flag actually stops the one lane that writes, and fails closed on an unreadable budget.

Already covered: scripts/setup-walk.mjs follows docs/open-source/self-hosting.md on a clean runner — it asserts the page still gives the commands it is about to run, copies .env.example, builds under SELF_HOSTED=true LOCAL_DB=true, starts the app and requests the page the reader is told to open, and parses the compose file — weekly and on any change to the quick-start surface (.github/workflows/setup-walk.yml), with a per-step verdict kept for 90 days.

Added .github/group-owners.json — one row per group in context-map.json with an owner CODEOWNERS already names, why a wrong change there costs something, and a triage rank — plus scripts/group-owners.mjs, which prints the join (which CODEOWNERS law files land inside which group, and which groups contain none) and whose G1..G5 checks block on every build via test-unit/group-owners.test.mjs, so a group a rescan adds cannot land unclaimed.

lessons: This repository answers most maturity gaps before they are raised — post-deploy verification, a cold setup walk, and an enforcement index for its prose rules all already exist and are wired. Read AGENTS.md, .github/constraint-map.json and the workflow list BEFORE assuming a gap is open; several of these items were closed by prior work the scanner did not sample.

Its house idiom for a new control is a triple, and copying it is what makes a change land: a declaration in .github/*.json (with a $cannotSee list saying what it does not prove), a zero-dependency script in scripts/ that prints the join, and a blocking test-unit census that fails when the declaration stops describing the tree. The measurement reports; the inventory blocks.

Every number that decides what red means is pinned twice — in the script that enforces it and in .github/contract-ledger.json with a dated reason — so raising a floor is a two-file diff or the build goes red. Budget for that whenever widening a measure.

Adding a stage to check:ci is expensive here: test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs demands a matching rule row in the map AND the AGENTS.md table, gate-remedy.test.mjs demands a remedy entry, and gates:timings:check re-checks cheapest-first ordering. Wiring a new check through test:unit instead avoids all three and is equally blocking.

An offline lane cannot establish a baseline, and this repository forbids inventing one (tsconfig.strict.json, .github/typecheck-strict.json). Prefer changes whose green-on-arrival state is verifiable by reading committed files — a catalogue anchor, a declaration's shape — over anything that needs a count somebody has to measure first.
